I read the whole file and the parallel Injective/Presentation.lean. I also grepped for uses of the one simp lemma and for Mathlib's projectivePresentationOfMapProjectivePresentation and injectivePresentationOfMap.

The only simp-interface item is `projective_iff_projective_obj_of_finite_paths`, marked `@[simp]`. It rewrites `Projective M` for `M` in the `IsFinDim` full subcategory to `Projective M.obj`. That is the right direction: it goes to the ambient object, so `M.obj` becomes the underlying representation and the rewrite cannot loop. The injective file has the same `@[simp]` pattern, so the two are consistent. I found no competing Mathlib simp lemma for `Projective` on `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`. The instance arguments (`Finite (TotalPath Q)` and `Small`) are ordinary instances that simp can synthesise. The two uses I found in AuslanderReiten/Sequence.lean apply the lemma through `.mp` and `.mpr`, so I saw no downstream effect from the attribute.

The `simpa only [...]` calls unfold Mathlib's `Equivalence.projectivePresentationOfMapProjectivePresentation`. A missing `.p` simp lemma would be Mathlib's responsibility, not this file's, and the local proof works. This is too minor to report under the rubric.

I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out unseen simp interactions. I found none that I could support from the sources.
